sources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations

folds.text: An **evaluation**, or eval, is a repeatable test of how good AI output is. It beats a gut feeling, because you can run it again after every change.
Start by deciding what good means. Criteria should be **specific** and **measurable**. "Good performance" is vague. "Gets the sentiment right" can be checked.
Build tests that mirror real use. Include odd cases too, like very long input, unclear requests and things people should not ask.
Grade automatically when you can: an exact match, a code check, or another model as the grader. Use a different model from the one that wrote the answer.
More tests, even roughly graded, beat a few perfect ones. Judge on several things at once, such as accuracy, tone, and speed.

folds.question: Which success criterion is the best one?
options: Correct label on nearly every item in a labelled test set
folds.why: It is specific and measurable, so you can test it again and again.
